bare-bones.short: When you choose not to equip armor, you have a base Armor Score of {{strengthPlus3|#|3 + your Strength}} and use these base damage thresholds:

forceful-push:
Make an attack with your primary weapon against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal damage and knock them back to Close range. On a success with Hope, add a d6 to your damage roll.
You can also spend a Hope to make them temporarily Vulnerable.
i-am-your-shield: When an ally within Very Close range would take damage, mark a Stress to stand in the way and become the target of the attack instead. When you take damage from it, you can mark any number of Armor Slots.
body-basher: On a successful attack with a Melee-range weapon, gain {{strength|a +# bonus to your damage roll|a bonus to your damage roll equal to your Strength}}.
bold-presence:
When you make a Presence Roll, spend a Hope to add {{strength|#|your Strength}} to the roll.
Once per rest, when you would gain a condition, describe how your bold presence helps and avoid gaining it.
critical-inspiration: Once per rest, when you critically succeed on an attack, all allies within Very Close range can clear a Stress or gain a Hope.
lean-on-me: Once per long rest, when you console or inspire an ally who failed an action roll, you both clear 2 Stress.
goad-them-on: Describe how you taunt a target within Close range, then make a Presence Roll against them. On a success, they mark a Stress, and the next time the GM spotlights them, they must target you with an attack made with disadvantage.
support-tank: When an ally within Close range fails a roll, spend 2 Hope to let them reroll their Hope or Fear Die.
armorer:
While wearing armor, gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Score.
When you repair your armor as a downtime move during a rest, your allies also clear an Armor Slot.
rousing-strike: Once per rest, when you critically succeed on an attack, you and all allies who can see or hear you can clear a Hit Point or 1d4 Stress.
inevitable: When you fail an action roll, your next action roll has advantage.
rise-up:
Gain {{proficiency|a +# bonus|a bonus equal to your Proficiency}} to your Severe threshold.
When you mark 1 or more Hit Points from an attack, clear a Stress.
shrug-it-off: When you would take damage, mark a Stress to reduce the severity by one threshold, then roll a d6. On a 3 or lower, place this card in your vault.
valor-touched:
When 4 or more loadout cards are from the Valor domain, gain:
- +1 bonus to your Armor Score
- When you mark 1 or more Hit Points without marking an Armor Slot, clear an Armor Slot.
full-surge: Once per long rest, mark 3 Stress to push your body to its limits: gain a +2 bonus to all your traits until your next rest.
ground-pound: Spend 2 Hope to strike the ground and make a Strength Roll against all targets within Very Close range. Targets you succeed against are thrown back to Far range and make a Reaction Roll (17); those who fail take 4d10+8 damage, and those who succeed take half.
hold-the-line:
Describe your defensive stance and spend a Hope. If an adversary moves within Very Close range, they’re pulled into Melee range and Restrained.
This lasts until you move or fail a roll with Fear, or the GM spends 2 Fear on their turn to clear it.
lead-by-example: When you deal damage to an adversary, mark a Stress and describe how you encourage your allies. The next PC to attack that adversary can clear a Stress or gain a Hope.
unbreakable: When you mark your last Hit Point, instead of making a death move, roll a d6 and clear Hit Points equal to the result. Then place this card in your vault.
unyielding-armor: When you would mark an Armor Slot, roll {{proficiency|#d6|a number of d6s equal to your Proficiency}}. If any roll a 6, reduce the severity by one threshold without marking an Armor Slot.
